Liverpool kept back-to-back clean sheets under Andoni Iraola for the first time this week

A year has passed, and there has been a world of change at Liverpool .

Thursday marked 12 months since the Reds lost 4-1 to PSV Eindhoven at Anfield in the Champions League, the culmination of their worst run of results in more than 70 years.

By the time the final whistle blew that night there were some boos, but Anfield was half empty and belief from the fanbase had evaporated as Liverpool lost for the ninth time in 12 games.

Arne Slot's side had won the Premier League title the season before, but that game against the Dutch side was arguably the nadir of his second campaign in charge. Steven Gerrard said that evening that Liverpool "just keep bleeding".

The bleeding did stop somewhat, and Liverpool qualified for the Champions League, but it was a campaign that left Slot wounded and, come the end of the campaign, he was sacked.

Everyone has moved on in one way or another. The PSV game is in the distant past now.

And after a dizzying few days where Liverpool have scored seven without reply across the Premier League and Champions League, beating Manchester United and Club Brugge, Andoni Iraola's side are giving fans reasons to start believing again.

That is just as well, because Sunday is derby day against Everton .

"You can really see this manager stamping his philosophy and his way of playing on the team," former Liverpool captain Gerrard said on BBC Radio 5 Live this week.

"They are playing a lot faster, a lot more intense, playing a lot more vertical and getting it forward a lot quicker.

"It's a lot more exciting to watch than it was at the back end of last season."

Everton and Liverpool fans debate Sunday's Merseyside derby

When Liverpool lost to Arsenal at the start of November, they were threatening in phases against the reigning champions but finished the game without a shot on target - despite starting with three attacking players who cost more than £100m each.

But they have now scored 10 goals in their past three games, with that trio of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola delivering 10 goal involvements between them.

Both Isak and Wirtz are in their best form since making the move to Liverpool in 2025 and both spoke in Bruges this week about how good they are feeling. Isak has four goals in his past four matches while Wirtz has scored in each of his past three.

"It's a dream situation for Wirtz now," said Gerrard.

"Under Iraola, he has given him more freedom, more licence to take risks and to be the difference maker."

Combined, Wirtz and Isak have surpassed their total goal involvements from last season and, alongside the likes of Barcola, Cody Gakpo, Victor Munoz, Rio Ngumoha and Hugo Ekitike - once he returns from injury in January - Liverpool have a youthful and vibrant attack that can rattle fear into defences across Europe.

"It's not just about those two [Isak and Wirtz]. If we play well, someone will score," said Iraola. "If we have more chances then the opposition, someone will score."

Iraola will also be pleased that his midfielders are getting high up the pitch and scoring too, with Alexis Mac Allister and Dominik Szoboszlai getting nine goals between them this season.

The challenge now is for the frontline to deliver consistently and crucially, in those games against the best opposition. In the Champions League, Liverpool have scored 17 times in five games, but it hasn't gone unnoticed that they failed to score once across 180 minutes against Manchester City and Arsenal .

Isak and Wirtz in a 'good place' - Iraola

Like he did against LASK, Iraola opted to rest Virgil van Dijk against Club Brugge and the centre-back duo of Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo helped to keep a clean sheet. From the eye test alone, Liverpool are looking more assured defensively and Araujo's ability to fill in across the backline is a big part of that.

Admittedly, they have failed to replace the attacking quality that Trent Alexander-Arnold provided, but Araujo is a trusted option and a fan favourite while left-back Milos Kerkez is finding his feet under Iraola after a difficult first campaign. Iraola said Wednesday's game against Brugge was Kerkez's best display of the season.

Van Dijk and Jacquet in particular have excelled, while Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni are on their way back from injuries.

Liverpool conceded 53 goals in the Premier League last season, their most in a 38-game campaign in the competition, and it looked like nothing had changed when they conceded twice against both Newcastle and Nottingham Forest in their first two games this season.

But since then they have kept clean sheets against Ipswich , Fulham , Bournemouth , high-scoring Brighton and Manchester United .

And it is worth noting that under the guidance of Tommy Elphick, one of Iraola's assistants responsible for defensive set-pieces, and Lewis Mahoney, the set-piece analyst, Liverpool are no longer conceding for fun.

It is still an area opposition teams are targeting, and they have conceded four non-penalty set-piece goals in the Champions League and EFL Cup, but their rate of 2.3 xG (expected goals) conceded per 100 opposition corners is the best in the Premier League.

It was quite the sight to see Iraola deliver Jurgen Klopp-style fist pumps with a smile in front of the Kop after Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United .

"It's not something that I normally do," he said. "But in that moment I felt like everyone was expecting, and I think we were all celebrating."

His side were rampant - albeit against a poor United side who were down to 10 men early on - and could easily have scored more if they were ruthless.

With the Merseyside derby next on Sunday and a chance to close the gap to four points on Arsenal , before the Gunners take on Manchester City later in the afternoon, Iraola will be keen to temper expectations.

Any talk of a title challenge seems premature, and Iraola is of the belief that you must wait until halfway through the campaign before "thinking and understanding" the table - but Liverpool are a side on the up.

From all of the managerial changes in the summer, Iraola has arguably had the strongest start, with his replacement at Bournemouth , Marco Rose, impressing too.

Fixtures come thick and fast now, with three games in the space of seven days coming up, starting with the short trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium. Liverpool host Sunderland on Wednesday before going to Chelsea next Saturday.

"To enjoy it, there is only one way: to win the game," Iraola said on Friday.

It is early doors, but the Anfield hierarchy wanted a fresh beginning when he was appointed and, after a stuttering start, confidence is rising under the Spaniard.

Win against their arch rivals on Sunday and that optimism will only grow.

Jamie Miller has equalled the six-week streak set by Dave Edmunds' I Hear You Knocking in 1970

Jamie Miller's Babydoll has become the longest-running UK number one single by a Welsh artist in 56 years.

Miller, who is originally from Pontprennau in Cardiff, claimed the top spot with his TikTok-viral hit for the sixth consecutive week on Friday.

The 29-year-old star's success is equal to the six-week streak set by Dave Edmunds' I Hear You Knocking back in 1970.

Babydoll was released on 7 August - just months after Miller considered quitting music - and exploded after actress Jennifer Love Hewitt and other stars posted videos which featured the track.

The song snowballed on social media and led to a viral dance, his first UK top 10 single , and reached number one in the US iTunes pop chart.

Miller is the first Welsh artist since 2011 to earn a UK Number 1 single - after Sian Evans' feature on DJ Fresh's Louder.

He is also the first solo male Welsh artist in 41 years to top the singles chart, after Shakin' Stevens' 1985 timeless festive hit, Merry Christmas Everyone.

Following the achievement, Miller said "nothing feels normal" anymore , but he was trying to "live in the moment" as he comes to terms with his history-making song.

The success transformed his career, but he said his "made it" moment was telling his taxi driver dad and cleaner mum they could retire.

"Be delusional with your dreams," says Jamie Miller

Miller, who grew up in Cardiff but has lived in Los Angeles for about nine years, launched his career nearly a decade ago as a 19-year-old, after coming third on the sixth season of The Voice UK.

He also recorded a separate version of Babydoll with Off Campus star Antonio Cipriano , after initially joking about the idea on social media.

Cipriano told BBC Wales Miller was "one of the best vocalists I've ever heard", adding he had been a fan of Miller's voice "for years".

Sir Elton John previously said he was "leaping around the kitchen" when he first heard Miller's history-making single.

Speaking on Sir Elton's Rocket Hour podcast, the Rocket Man singer told Miller he had a "huge future".

Jamie Miller (right) and Off Campus star Antonio Cipriano recorded a version of Babydoll together after a joke on social media

Miller praised his mum, Anne, for her unwavering support.

He said, during his childhood, other boys were interested in football and rugby, and there was "bullying" that came with pursuing singing.

But he said his mum would encourage him to "just to ignore people and to keep going".

Miller said he was working on a "soulful, joyous and happy album that I feel like I've waited my whole life to write", and hopes it will be released at the beginning of 2027.

Last week, Miller released his take on the festive classic It's Beginning To Look A Lot Like Christmas.

In addition, the singer is currently planning a world tour, with a promise to return to his roots and perform a number of shows in Wales.

It has emerged that Roi Herzog was among the 36-member entourage

One of the many sessions Uganda’s President Yoweri Museveni has had with the Congolese leader Felix Tshisekedi (left)

For years, President Félix Tshisekedi’s survival strategy has rested on a single, exhausted reflex of blaming Kigali for every governance failure, military defeat and internal fracture inside the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

Yet in late 2026, that narrative is unraveling, not because of anything Kigali said or did, but because Uganda has finally broken its silence.

Recent pronouncements from Kampala’s top military leadership, including Chief of Defence Forces General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, have shattered Kinshasa’s carefully curated script.

Kampala has openly voiced alarm over the relentless persecution of Hema and Tutsi communities in Ituri and the Kivus by the Congolese armed forces-FARDC and their coalition of proxy militias, specifically the Wazalendo network, the genocidal FDLR, Nyatura factions such as CMC-FDP, APCLS and NDC-R, Mai-Mai groups, and CODECO, while preparing to push toward Isiro to neutralize Musa Baluku’s Allied Democratic Forces-ADF.

More significantly, Uganda has signaled a pragmatic openness toward the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), the broad coalition led by former President Joseph Kabila that absorbed the M23/AFC and Twirwaneho in October 2026, recognizing that the FRN is maintaining civil order and protecting vulnerable minorities where the Congolese state has failed.

This shift exposes a glaring contradiction in Kinshasa’s diplomacy. Why does Tshisekedi obsessively attack Rwanda on every international stage while cautiously whispering around Uganda?

Even after summoning Kampala’s envoy in November 2026 over General Kainerugaba’s remarks, Kinshasa avoided the venomous demonization it routinely reserves for Kigali.

The answer lies in sheer political cowardice and domestic vulnerability. Tshisekedi’s government depends on Uganda’s military presence under Operation Shujaa to contain the ADF and keep northern trade corridors alive.

Moreover, anti-Rwandan xenophobia is an easy domestic distraction for a president losing legitimacy at home, whereas confronting Uganda openly would expose the total collapse of Kinshasa’s authority across the entire eastern frontier.

Meanwhile, Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye offers a masterclass in blundering geopolitical calculation and active complicity in war crimes.

While Uganda has chosen the side of regional consensus and civilian protection, Gitega has quietly entrenched thousands of Burundian troops in South Kivu in support of the FARDC, Wazalendo militias and the genocidal FDLR, effectively undermining the very peace initiatives it claims to support.

Earlier in 2026, Ndayishimiye infamously washed his hands of his troops’ conduct, claiming they operate under Kinshasa’s command and cannot be questioned over links to the FDLR. Today, as the FRN consolidates governance and Kampala demands inclusive regional talks, Ndayishimiye’s actions speak volumes.

Refusing to pick a principled side is itself a choice. But worse, he has chosen to prop up a failing regime in Kinshasa and shield genocidal elements rather than face the reality of a new regional order.

Ultimately, Tshisekedi’s external distraction campaign cannot mask the fact that he is increasingly unwanted in his own country. Having alienated the population of eastern DRC, driven former head of state Joseph Kabila to lead a unified politico-military opposition, and outsourced national defense to foreign mercenaries, Kinshasa has lost both moral and territorial authority. Distant diplomatic tracks in Washington and Doha have failed precisely because they failed to hold him to his word.

As Uganda rightly recognizes, durable peace will never come from anti-Rwanda slogans; it requires bringing Kinshasa, the FRN and Congolese stakeholders to the table under East African Community and SADC mechanisms.

Gary Barlow, Mark Owen and Howard Donald said their 10th number one album felt as special as their first

Take That have landed their 10th number one album, securing their spot as one of the most successful British bands in Official Chart history.

The Manchester group, made up of Gary Barlow, Howard Donald and Mark Owen, topped the UK album chart with Dreamers.

The group first scored a number one record more than three decades ago with their second studio album Everything Changes.

The band told Official Charts: "Thank you so much to everybody who has supported Dreamers, it means the world to us to see people embracing this album.

"Thinking back to our first number one with Everything Changes in 1993, this one today feels even more special.

"The fact that we can still reach these heights after 30 years is a feat not lost on us, and we wouldn't be here without our incredibly dedicated fans."

Take That's 10th studio album also secured the biggest opening week for a group in 2026 so far, outselling the rest of the top 10 combined.

The band now tie with Queen and Coldplay as the groups with 10 number one albums, with only The Beatles and The Rolling Stones boasting more chart-topping LPs among British bands.

Take That (left to right Howard Donald, Gary Barlow, Mark Owen and Jason Orange) a week after announcing they were splitting up in 1996

They are also one of just five groups to have topped the Official Albums Chart in each of the past four decades, alongside Blur, Oasis, Stereophonics and Steps.

The group previously topped the charts in 2023 with This Life.

The British boyband, known for the songs Back For Good, Pray and Shine, rose to fame in the 90s, and also featured Robbie Williams and Jason Orange.

Williams left the group in 1995 to pursue a solo career and Orange left in 2014.

Asked how the band would be celebrating the album hitting the top spot, Barlow said: "Let's go to the seaside and get fish and chips - and an ice cream."
